![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/70dc1594c0072b83429fc1f5d6be4fa454f6650c3eeef37c41c2d3ec691bb35f.png)

Consider the region bounded by the curve $y=x^2$ and the horizontal line $y=-1$ from $x=0$ to $x=1,$ as shown in the picture. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $360^{\circ}$about the line $y=-1.$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, note that the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1$ along the $x$-axis.

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/3b0427e7d37245d86d347d6d4f867ae3d17e5f0a030feb53d28ad4bbc856f85c.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=-1,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=x^2.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

 

$$
\eqalign{
	V &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left({\color{blue}\textrm{upper function}}\right) - \left({\color{brown}\textrm{lower function}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \[5pt]
	 	&= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[\: {\color{blue}x^2 }- \left({\color{brown}-1} \right)\:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x \[5pt]  
                &= \pi\int_{0}^{1} (x^2+1)^2 \, \textrm{d}x \[5pt]
		&= \pi\int_{0}^{1} (x^4+2x^2+1) \, \textrm{d}x \[5pt]
		&= \pi \left(\dfrac{x^5}{5}+\dfrac{2x^3}{3}+x \right) \Bigg|_{0}^{1} \[5pt]
		&= \pi \left( \left[ \dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{2}{3}+1 \right] - 0 \right) \[5pt]
		&= \dfrac{28 \pi}{15}.
}
$$
